Rashi on Nedarim 42b:1:1.hebrew: שאני הכא דאמר בחייו ובמותו - אבל היכא דאמר בסתם, אימא לעולם אין אדם אוסר וכו':
Rashi on Nedarim 42b:1:1.english: It is different here, as he said, "During his lifetime and upon his death" - But where he spoke without specification, I would say [that] indeed a person cannot prohibit [something after it leaves his possession], etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 42b:2:1.hebrew: מ"מ קשיא - כדאמרינן, אי בהאי טעמא פליגי, ליפלגו בנכסים אלו:
Rashi on Nedarim 42b:2:1.english: In any case, [it is] difficult - As we said, if they disagree regarding this reason, let them disagree regarding "this property" [as well].

Rashi on Nedarim 42b:2:2.hebrew: אלא בנכסים אלו כ"ע לא פליגי - דמשמע נכסים אלו לעולם:
Rashi on Nedarim 42b:2:2.english: Rather, in [the case of] "this property," no one disagrees - For "this property" implies [that the prohibition lasts] forever.

Rashi on Nedarim 42b:2:3.hebrew: כי פליגי דאמר נכסי - ר' יוחנן ור"ל סברי: היכא דאמר "נכסי", אין אדם אוסר וכו', ד"נכסי" משמע כל זמן שהן ברשותי. ורב ושמואל סברי: אפילו אמר "נכסי", (אמר) אדם אוסר דבר וכו':
Rashi on Nedarim 42b:2:3.english: When they disagree [is] where he said "my property" - Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish hold [that] where he said "my property," a person cannot prohibit, etc., for "my property" implies as long as it is in my possession. And Rav and Shmuel hold [that] even if he said "my property," a person can prohibit something, etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 42b:4:1.hebrew: קונם לתוך ביתך שאני נכנס - כל זמן שהוא ביתך, דהוי דומיא דנכסי עליך; כיון שמת בעה"ב או שמכרו לאותו בית לאחר, מותר ליכנס בו, דהשתא אינו שלו. אבל אמר לבית זה שאני נכנס, דהוי משמע נכסים אלו — דקא אסר הבית עליו לעולם — אע"פ שמת או מכרו לאחר, אסו' ליכנס בו. אלמא דשאני בין נכסי לנכסים, והיכי קאמרי רב ושמואל ל"ש נכסי ול"ש נכסים דאדם אוסר וכו':
Rashi on Nedarim 42b:4:1.english: Konam [that] I enter into your house - [This means] as long as it is your house, which is similar to [saying] "my property [is forbidden] to you"; once the homeowner has died or sold that house to another, it is permitted to enter it, for now it is not his. However, [if] he said, "[Entering] this house that I enter [is konam]," which implies "this property" — for he prohibits the house upon himself forever — even though [the owner] died or sold it to another, it is forbidden to enter it. Apparently, there is a difference between "my property" and "[this] property"; so how can Rav and Shmuel say [that] there is no difference [whether he says] "my property" and no difference [whether he says] "[this] property," that a person can prohibit, etc.?

Rashi on Nedarim 42b:5:1.english: Rather, when Rav and Shmuel stated [their ruling]:

Rashi on Nedarim 42b:7:1.hebrew: בעומדים אילנות על הגבולין - לחוץ, שיכול לתלוש מן הפירות מבחוץ, מש"ה אינו יורד; דהא דרחמנא אפקריה לארעא גבי שביעית לצורך אכילה, ועכשיו לא היה נכנס לצורך אכילה:
Rashi on Nedarim 42b:7:1.english: Where trees are standing on the borders - [extending] outward, so that he can pluck from the fruits from outside; therefore he may not go down [into the field], for that which the Merciful One rendered the land ownerless regarding the Sabbatical year [was] for the purpose of eating, whereas now he would not be entering for the purpose of eating.

Rashi on Nedarim 42b:7:2.hebrew: ר"ש בן אליקים אמר - הא דקתני אוכל מן הנוטות, ודאי כדקאמרת, כגון דעומדין על הגבולין, משום שיכול להושיט ידו וליקח מבחוץ. אבל אין עומדין על הגבולין, אינו יורד לתוך שדהו, דאסור לו לירד לשם:
Rashi on Nedarim 42b:7:2.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim said - That which [the Mishnah] teaches, "he may eat from the overhanging [branches]," [is] certainly as you say, such as where they are standing on the borders, because he can stretch out his hand and take from the outside. However, [if] they are not standing on the borders, he may not go down into his field, for it is forbidden for him to go down there.

Rashi on Nedarim 42b:7:3.hebrew: גזירה שמא ישהא בעמידה - דלאחר שאכל עומד לו לשם, וקמיתהני מנכסים דמדיר, ואסור. דהאי דאפקריה רחמנא, כל זמן שהוא אוכל — אז יכול לעמוד לשם, דהפקר הוא, אבל שלא לצורך אכילה לא אפקריה:
Rashi on Nedarim 42b:7:3.english: A decree lest he remain standing - For after he has eaten, he stands there, and he derives benefit from the property of the one who made the vow, and [that] is forbidden. For [regarding] that which the Merciful One declared [it] ownerless: as long as he is eating, then he may stand there, for it is ownerless; but not for the purpose of eating, He did not declare it ownerless.

Rashi on Nedarim 42b:8:1.hebrew: המודר הנאה מחבירו לא ישאיל לו - שאלה בכלים, הלואה במעות:
Rashi on Nedarim 42b:8:1.english: One who is prohibited by a vow from benefiting from his fellow may not lend to him - Borrowing [applies] to utensils; lending [applies] to money.

Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:2:1.hebrew: מכל מקום [קשיא] - אי ס"ל דאין אדם אוסר דבר שלא ברשותו, לשמעינן מילתיה באלו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:2:1.english: In any case, [it is] difficult - If he holds that a person cannot forbid something that is not in his possession, let him teach us his statement regarding "these [properties]":

Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:2:2.hebrew: אלא בנכסי אלו לא פליגי דאדם אוסר כי פליגי בנכסי דרב ושמואל סברי ל"ש נכסי אלו לא שנא נכסי אוסר - וקשה: אמאי נקט במילתיה "נכסי אלו"? הוה מצי למיפרך מהך ברייתא דלעיל: "קונם שאתה נהנה, מת — יירשנו", אלמא בנכסי אינו אוסר; או מהאי דלעיל (נדרים דף לה.) גבי קורדום: "מת או נתנו במתנה — מותר". מיהו ניחא ליה טפי לאותובי ממתניתין דלקמן, דדמי טפי ל"נכסי אלו" דקתני:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:2:2.english: "Rather, in [the case of] 'this property' they do not disagree, for a person renders [it] forbidden; when they disagree, it is in [the case of] 'my property,' for Rav and Shmuel hold that there is no difference [between] 'this property' and 'my property,' [in both cases] he renders [it] forbidden" - And it is difficult: Why did [the Gemara] mention "this property" in its statement? It could have raised an objection from that baraita above: "Konam that you benefit [from me] — [if] he died, he inherits him," thus [proving that] with "my property" one does not render [it] forbidden; or from that [Mishnah] above (Nedarim 35a) regarding an axe: "[If] he died or gave it as a gift, it is permitted." However, it was preferable for [the Gemara] to raise an objection from the Mishnah below, because it is more similar to "this property" that it teaches:

Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:4:1.hebrew: מי איכא למ"ד דבנכסי אדם אוסר - והתנן בפ' השותפין — מותר, דלא נאסר אלא בעודהו ברשותו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:4:1.english: Is there anyone who says that with "my property" a person renders [it] forbidden - But didn't we learn in the chapter [entitled] HaShutafin — [it is] permitted, for it is forbidden only while it is still in his possession.

Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:5:1.english: Rather, when Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish said [their statement, it was] regarding "my property"; Rav and Shmuel [said theirs] regarding "this property" - And they do not disagree.

Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:6:1.hebrew: מאי שנא דאוכל מן הנוטות - דפירי דהפקירא אינון, ארעא נמי הפקירא הוא, ואפקרה רחמנא לצורך אכילה; ואמאי לא ירד בה לאכול מאותן שאינן נוטות:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:6:1.english: What is different [about the Sabbatical Year] that he eats from the [branches] that lean out? - [It is] because the fruits are ownerless; [and] the land is also ownerless, for the Merciful One rendered it ownerless for the purpose of eating, so why may he not enter it to eat from those [fruits] that do not lean out?

Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:7:1.hebrew: בעומדים על הגבולין - דיכול לתולשן בלא ירידה בתוך השדה, ולכך אמר דלא ירד לתוך השדה כיון דאפשר לאוכלם בלא ירידה; אבל היכא דאין עומדין על הגבולין, לעולם יורד ואוכל, דרחמנא אפקריה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:7:1.english: Where [the trees] are standing on the borders - For he can pluck them without going down into the field, and therefore [the Tanna] said that he may not go down into the field, since it is possible to eat them without going down; but where they are not standing on the borders, he may always go down and eat, for the Merciful One rendered it ownerless.

Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:7:2.hebrew: אלא גזירה שמא ירבה בעמידה - לאחר אכילה. ולצורך אכילה אפקריה רחמנא, שלא לצורך אכילה — לא; ואינו מותר אלא בנוטות, שנוטות מחוץ לשדה, ואינו נכנס לתוך השדה כלל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:7:2.english: "Rather, [it is] a decree lest he prolong standing" - after eating. And [it is] for the purpose of eating [that] the Merciful One declared it ownerless; [when it is] not for the purpose of eating, [He did] not. And he is only permitted [to eat] from overhanging [branches], which lean outside the field, and he does not enter into the field at all.

Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:8:1.hebrew: המודר הנאה מחבירו - שחבירו הדירו שלא יהנה משלו. לא ישאילנו חבירו, דקא מהני ליה; ולא ישאל מחבירו — ובגמרא פריך: הא לא מהני ליה למודר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:8:1.english: One who is forbidden by vow [to derive] benefit from his fellow - [Meaning] that his fellow imposed a vow upon him that he may not benefit from what is his. His fellow may not lend [an item] to him, because he [thereby] benefits him; nor may he borrow from his fellow [the one forbidden by the vow] — and in the Gemara it asks: Surely he is not benefiting the one forbidden by the vow!

Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:8:2.english: And his fellow may not lend [money] to him - For he benefits him.

Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:8:3.english: Nor may his fellow borrow from him - And in the Gemara it asks: Why?

Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:8:4.hebrew: לא ימכור לו חבירו - דאמרינן בשילהי פירקין דלעיל (נדרים דף לא.) דמיתהני מוכר ללוקח, ולכך אסור בין למוכר בין ללוקח:
Tosafot on Nedarim 42b:8:4.english: His fellow may not sell to him - For we say at the end of the previous chapter (Nedarim 31a) that a seller derives benefit from a buyer [and vice versa], and therefore it is forbidden both for the seller and for the buyer.
